The previous week's figure was revised higher to 212,000 from 209,000.

The data suggest that employers continue to hold onto workers despite signs of moderation.

Initial claims remain well below levels typically associated with a deteriorating labor market, reinforcing the view that layoffs are still relatively scarce.

Continuing claims, which measure the number of people already receiving unemployment benefits, rose to 1.799 million, above the 1.790 million expected.

The prior week's figure was also revised higher to 1.781 million from 1.777 million.

Overall, the data points to some stabilisation after the strengthening seen in the prior months.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

Scoreboard update: An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics.

Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.
